title: He Stood There With All Authority… And Still Chose You
paragraphs:
He Stood There With All Authority… And Still Chose You
The hidden weight of Matthew 28:18 that most believers feel… but rarely understand
He didn’t whisper it.
He didn’t hesitate.
There was no trembling in His voice, no uncertainty in His stance, no shadow of doubt in His eyes.
After betrayal… after abandonment… after nails tore through His flesh and a spear confirmed His death… after the silence of the grave was broken by resurrection power—
He stood.
And He said it.

“ἐδόθη μοι πᾶσα ἐξουσία ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.”
Edothē moi pasa exousia en ouranō kai epi tēs gēs.
“All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.” (Matthew 28:18)
Let that sit in your chest for a second.
Not some authority.
Not partial authority.
Not borrowed power that could be taken back.

πᾶσα ἐξουσία — pasa exousia — means total, complete, unrestricted dominion. The kind of authority that doesn’t ask permission. The kind that doesn’t negotiate with darkness. The kind that doesn’t bend to fear, sin, shame, or your past.
Everything.

In heaven… where angels tremble at His voice.
On earth… where broken people like us are still trying to understand grace.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.
Because if He truly has all authority…
Then what are we still holding onto?

The Greek word ἐδόθη (edothē) — “has been given” — is in the aorist passive tense. It points to a decisive, completed act. This wasn’t gradual. This wasn’t evolving. This was established. Declared. Sealed.
The Son, who humbled Himself to the point of death, was now exalted with absolute authority (Philippians 2:8–11).
But He didn’t say this to intimidate them.
He said it to send them.
That’s the part many people skip.
Authority wasn’t the end of the statement—it was the foundation for what came next.
Because right after declaring His absolute dominion… He gave a command.
“Go.”

Not when you feel ready.
Not when your life is clean.
Not when your doubts disappear.
Go.
Do you feel the tension?
Because many of us love the idea of Jesus having authority… until that authority reaches into our habits, our secrets, our pride, our hidden compromises.
We want Him as Savior… but hesitate when He steps in as Lord.
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected, didn’t it?
Because Matthew 28:18 is not just a declaration of power—it’s an invitation to surrender.
The Hebrew concept behind authority echoes words like מֶמְשָׁלָה (memshalah)—dominion, rule, governance. This isn’t cold control. It’s rightful kingship.
Jesus isn’t trying to dominate you.
He’s trying to restore you.
There’s a difference.
Because the same One who said “all authority is Mine”… is the One who washed feet.
The same One who holds dominion over heaven and earth… is the One who let Himself be crucified for you.
That’s the scandal.
That’s the paradox.
That’s the Gospel.

Authority wrapped in mercy.
Power expressed through sacrifice.
Kingship revealed through a cross.
And if He truly holds all authority… then your past doesn’t.

Your addiction doesn’t.
Your guilt doesn’t.
Your shame doesn’t.
Your failures don’t get the final say anymore.
He does.
So why are we still living like they do?
Why are we still negotiating with things He already defeated?
Why are we still listening to voices He already silenced?
If Jesus has all authority… then the only thing left for us is surrender.
Not partial surrender.
Not selective obedience.
Everything.
This is where transformation begins—not in perfection, but in honesty.
And maybe… just maybe… that’s why this verse hits differently when you really understand it.
Because it removes every excuse.
If He has all authority… then He has authority over your story.
Which means He can rewrite it.
Completely.
From scandal… to grace.
From brokenness… to redemption.
From who you were… to who He’s calling you to be.
And if this truth is awakening something inside you… don’t keep it to yourself.
Someone you love is still living like Jesus doesn’t have authority over their pain.
Because this isn’t just content.
This is discipleship.
And for those who want to go deeper…
If you truly want to glorify God, don’t just consume truth—help carry it.
Support the mission. Help spread the Gospel further than we ever could alone.
Because when truth changes you… it’s meant to move through you.
Ask yourself one question:
If Jesus has all authority… what in my life am I still refusing to surrender?
And don’t forget…
The One who holds all authority is still calling your name.
And He hasn’t given up on you.

Not then.
Not now.
Not ever.
Because the King who rules heaven and earth…
Still chose the cross for you.
And that changes everything.
